text:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: spike in 5xx + request timeouts observed for /v1/generate on us-east-1 gateway. p95 jumped from 120ms -> 1.6s, p99 -> 8.2s in last 3m. Error rate: 5xx 4.8% (baseline 0.2%). Incident created automatically. paging on-call.

maria: I'm the on-call SRE. looking... can someone confirm deploys in last 15m? @devon @alex

devon: pushed canary for api-gateway-mux 15m ago -> commit f3a9b2a. Rolling out 20% canary to prod pool. I see increase in gateway latency around 1839009600 (matches rollout).

alex: seeing same in traces. most errors = downstream timeouts to inference-service-v2 (grpc deadline exceeded). stack: gateway -> router -> inference-service-v2 (gpu-pool). p99 of inference-service-v2 CPU spikes and KV cache miss rate up.

sophia: tagging product: some customers report errors via support. initial estimate: 12 customers affected, burst duration ~5-8m so far. No major financial impact reported yet. classify P1? maria?

maria: P1 (customer-facing errors, broad surface). Paging incident commander and eng-runtime. @ops-shift are you available for handoff? :rotating_light:

ops-shift: here, standing by for handoff. what's the mitigation plan? prefer fast revert vs canary cutback? losing traffic due to timeouts.

devon: can quickly cut canary -> 0% to stop new traffic to that variant. But inference-service-v2 config change included a new dynamic batching patch that might be causing stalls under certain sequence-length distributions.

alex: logs (snip):
```
[1839009698] inference-service-v2: grpc: error: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
[1839009701] worker-7: kvcache miss ratio 44% (expected 5%)
[1839009702] gpu-util: 98% longest queue wait=720ms
```

sophia: customers on dedicated capacity? which tenants affected?

alex: mostly hosted API customers hitting longer prompts. embeddings unaffected.

devon: immediate mitigation steps I can do now:
- scale inference-service-v2 replica count +2 on hot nodes
- revert the canary rollout of gateway mux
- set short-term request timeout cut at gateway to 3s (was 10s) to fail fast

maria: do steps in that order and post commands. we want to reduce customer impact fast. prioritize revert if scaling doesn't show improvement in 2m.

devon: running scale now:
```
kubectl scale deployment inference-service-v2 --replicas=6 -n prod
```

(reacts: :white_check_mark:)

devon: scaling underway. also applying temporary gateway timeout override:
```
# feature flag: fast-fail-timeout
infractl set-config gateway.timeout_override_ms=3000 --env prod
```

alex: after scale + timeout change, p95 -> 420ms, p99 -> 1.2s, error rate down to 1.1% (still above baseline). Some queues drained but spikes persist.

maria: good improvement. given correlation with canary timestamp, please revert canary and re-observe. put traffic back to previous stable.

devon: reverting canary now:
```
deployctl promote --service gateway-mux --to-revision stable-2026-03-10
# or
kubectl rollout undo deployment/gateway-mux -n prod
```

(reacts: :hourglass_flowing_sand:)

devon: revert complete at 1839010200. Confirming no new canary pods.

alex: metrics after revert: p95 210ms, p99 420ms, error rate 0.25% — back near baseline. traces show successful fallthrough to inference-service-v1.

sophia: Ther's initial customer impact: ~30k API requests failed during spike window, about 0.05% of daily volume. Support updated status page: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1839009999

maria: incident commander update: cause likely regression in inference-service-v2 dynamic batching + gateway routing to canary. Next actions:
- rollback is confirmed, incident declared mitigated
- open a follow-up postmortem assigned to eng-runtime and eng-ml
- gather reproducer and add stricter canary SLO checks (p95/p99). Also add a canary throttling policy to avoid hitting kvcache cold thrash.

devon: filing PR to revert batching changes in v2 and add circuit-breaker + per-model concurrency limit. linking here when opened.

alex: capturing logs and traces for postmortem. saved snapshot to s3: s3://redwood-incident-archives/1839009999/snap.tar.gz

sophia: I've notified affected customers via support with a summary and ETA for root-cause. No SLA breaches expected but monitoring for escalations.

maria: passing to next on-call. ops-shift will monitor for 1h and escalate if anything reoccurs. @ops-shift take Handoff.

ops-shift: taking it. monitoring dashboards pinned to #oncall-dash. I'll follow up with postmortem link and owner. closing incident thread as mitigated but keeping it visible for 1h.

maria: thanks team. final note: retro action items - 1) stricter canary rollout gating, 2) add KV cache warming pre-rollout, 3) test dynamic batching under heavy long-sequence traffic in CI.

incident-bot: Incident 1839009999 marked mitigated by maria at 1839010400. Duration: ~7m. Notifications sent to incident channel and stakeholders.

ops-shift: handoff complete. monitoring OK at 1839010500. :white_check_mark:
_meta: generated for dataset: incident thread about timeout regression after deploy leading to rollback and handoff
